title: hx-push-url: Browser History API Synchronization & Back/Forward Cache

progressiveExplaining.eli5: When you click around a single-page app, the address bar at the top of your browser usually doesn't change, meaning you can't bookmark the page or click 'Back'. `hx-push-url` tells the browser to change the address bar to the new URL and remember the old screen so the browser's Back and Forward buttons work instantly.
progressiveExplaining.junior: `hx-push-url="true"` (or passing a specific path `hx-push-url="/contacts/1"`) updates the browser's address bar using `history.pushState()` when an HTMX request succeeds. HTMX snapshots the current DOM state into `localStorage` before swapping, so clicking the browser's Back button restores the previous view instantly without re-requesting the server.
progressiveExplaining.senior: Architecturally, `hx-push-url` bridges hypermedia partials with deep-linking and browser history navigation. HTMX intercepts `popstate` events on window back/forward navigation. It first attempts to restore the page from its internal DOM snapshot cache (`htmx-history-cache`). If the cached snapshot is missing or stale, it issues a background `HX-History-Restore-Request: true` fetch to the restored URL.
progressiveExplaining.underTheHood: When `hx-push-url` is active on an element, HTMX executes `saveHistoryCache()` before DOM swapping (saving the `innerHTML` of `document.body` to session storage keyed by URL). It calls `history.pushState({ htmx: true }, '', newUrl)`. On `popstate`, HTMX inspects `history.state`. If it finds a saved snapshot in cache, it restores `document.body.innerHTML` synchronously and triggers `htmx:historyRestore`.

interviewGotchas.question: What header can the server send to force a URL push even if the client didn't specify `hx-push-url`?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Interviewers test your knowledge of HTMX server response control headers.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: The server can send the **`HX-Push-Url: /new-url`** response header. This overrides client-side attributes and instructs HTMX to push `/new-url` onto the browser's history stack immediately upon swapping.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Sending `HX-Push-Url: false` explicitly prevents a URL from being pushed even if the client element had `hx-push-url="true"`.

interviewGotchas.question: Why does refreshing a page after `hx-push-url` sometimes render an unstyled partial instead of the full layout?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Checks understanding of the dual-purpose endpoint pattern.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer:
If a user navigates via HTMX (which sends `HX-Request: true`), the server returns a partial (`
Settings
`). If `hx-push-url="/tabs/settings"` updated the address bar, and the user hits **F5 (hard refresh)**, the browser sends a standard request *without* `HX-Request: true`. If the server blindly returns only the partial, the user sees broken unstyled HTML. The server must check for `HX-Request` and return the *full page shell* on direct requests.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Always wrap backend handlers in middleware that serves full layouts when `HX-Request` is absent.
